newsitem.title: USA: AMR says pilot dispute threatens company.
newsitem.headline: AMR says pilot dispute threatens company.

text.p: AMR Corp Chief Financial Officer Gerard Arpey said the labor dispute with pilots at American Airlines has left management fearing for the future of the carrier.

"We quite frankly are at a loss as to what to do next, accept a contract that would be at best uncompetitive versus our principal competitors, or a possible cessation of operations. Two disastrous sort of alternatives," Arpey said in a conference call with reporters.
Arpey said he had been at the company for 15 years and the current labor dispute with pilots was "as grave a situation as I've seen the company face in my career here."

Arpey said pilots had shown no sign of accepting binding arbitration in the dispute and he expects the National Mediation Board to put both sides into a 30-day "cooling off" period in their contract dispute as early as Wednesday night.
If no agreement is reached in that 30-day period, the union would be free to strike, while the carrier could implement new work conditions or simply lock out its pilots.

Arpey hoped mediators would broker a deal, but the pilots' latest proposal would leave American at a disadvantage of "hundreds of millions of dollars" against its competitors, United Airlines and Delta Air Lines.
